learning_outcomes.text: Students will be able to design isothermal flow reactors and batch reactors for homogeneous reactions.
They will be able to analyze kinetic data and determine the appropriate rate expression (reaction order and reaction rate expression).
They will be able to design steady-state and non-steady-state reactors using analytical techniques and computer programs.
They will be able to select the appropriate reactor or reactor system depending on reaction conditions.
They will be able to determine the necessary conditions to increase the selectivity of the desired product in multiple reactions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to chemical reaction engineering, Reaction Mechanism, Reaction rate concept, Concentration Concept and Conversion Rate
Collection and analysis of rate data (integral and differential methods)
Determination of reaction order, rate law and reaction rate constant
Initial rate method in the evaluation of experimental rate data
Creation of stoichiometric table, preparation for batch and flow reactors
General mole balance; Design and sizing of batch, continuous flow, and tubular reactors
Comparison of volumes of reactors and reactor systems
Reversible (Bidirectional) Reactions and kinetics, Chemical equilibrium
Yield and selectivity in Multiple Reactions
Isothermal and adiabatic reactor design: batch reactor and flow reactors
bibliography: Fogler H.S., “Elements of Chemical Reaction Engineering”, Pearson Education, Inc., Fifth Edition (2016).
Levenspiel, O., Chemical Reaction Engineering, John Wiley, Third Edition (1999).
Missen R.W., Mims C.A., Saville B.A., Introduction to chemical reaction engineering and kinetics, John Wiley (1999)
